mcu_g_12b_200000b0.name: hall_code_sample_12b
mcu_g_12b_200000b0.description: 12b build only. Hall code (0..7) read this tick by mcu_hall_transition_counter_update_v12b (FUN_08005D30) through FUN_08008F00. Codes 0 and 7 are invalid sector codes and are counted by a debounce (0x20000AC4 for code 7, 0x20000AD8 for codes other than 0 and 7). The debounce results raise event flags 0x400 (code 7 seen) and 0x80000 (valid code) in the event word at 0x20000AF8. Written every tick, never reset.

mcu_g_143_20000338.name: hall_pos_jump_143
mcu_g_143_20000338.description: 143 build only. Position-jump flag of the hall tracker (mcu_pos_tracker_update_v143, FUN_0800A580). It is set to 1 when the change between the two tracker samples at param_1[3] and param_1[5] has |delta| >= 0xF5C28F, cleared when the delta is within about +/-0x41892, and held in between. While it is set the tracker output (hall_pos_scaled_delta_143) is forced to 0x190000 and the holdoff counter hall_pos_holdoff_143 is cleared. Probably flags a mis-read hall edge or a wheel jump.

mcu_g_143_2000033c.name: hall_pos_scaled_delta_143
mcu_g_143_2000033c.description: 143 build only. Tracker output in signed Q16 units (probably the scaled rotor speed or position increment). It is computed from the sensor delta scaled by param_1[0x11] / 2^15, then clamped between the limits param_1[0xe] and param_1[0xf] and floored at 0x18000 when a flag in the tracker block is clear. While hall_pos_holdoff_143 is non-zero it is set to param_1[0xf]. While hall_pos_jump_143 is set it is 0x190000. Written every tick by mcu_pos_tracker_update_v143.

mcu_g_143_20000340.name: hall_pos_holdoff_143
mcu_g_143_20000340.description: 143 build only. Holdoff counter of the hall tracker in ticks. It is loaded with param_1[0xC] x 150 / 1000 (probably 15 percent of a configured window) when the sensor delta is between 0x3126E9 and 0x2666669, decremented once per tick while the delta is below 0x3126E9, and cleared when the delta reaches 0x2666669. While it is non-zero the tracker output is held at param_1[0xF]. Telemetry request 0x344 sends it (0x20000310 and 0x20000311).

mcu_g_0160_20000678.name: hall_code_prev
mcu_g_0160_20000678.description: Hall code (0..7, bits 9..11 of hall_status_word) of the previous dispatch. mcu_hall_state_dispatch (0x08003034) calls the handler for the current code with the argument prev XOR current, then stores the current code here. The value is set on every tick and is not reset.

mcu_g_0160_20000698.name: hall_handler_table
mcu_g_0160_20000698.description: Table of 8 handler function pointers, one per current hall code. mcu_hall_state_dispatch (0x08003034) calls entry [current code] with the argument (previous code XOR current code), which is the set of hall bits that changed. The table sits in RAM, so it is probably filled at startup from flash; that copy is not in the decompiled code of this packet.

mcu_g_0160_20000714.name: hall_sector_angle_table
mcu_g_0160_20000714.description: Electrical angle for each 3-bit hall code, in Q16 units where a full turn is 0x6487E. Indexed by the code returned from the hall reader in mcu_hall_position_update (0x08009598), FUN_08009160, FUN_08008F34 and FUN_080093F8. A negative entry (probably the invalid codes 0 and 7) is treated as a sensor fault in FUN_08009160, which sets fault code 7. The count of 8 is inferred from the 3-bit index, not from a bound check in the code.

mcu_g_0160_20001fda.name: hall_status_word
mcu_g_0160_20001fda.description: Drive state word shared by many modules. Bits 9..11 are the current hall code (0..7), read by mcu_hall_state_dispatch and by the hall tracking code. Bit 0 drives the PC8 indicator and bit 1 the PB2 indicator (mcu_indicator_update); bits 7..8 drive PC11 and bit 12 drives PB6 (mcu_status_drive_pb6_pc11); bit 14 drives PC12 (mcu_hall_dispatch_pc12_output); bit 15 is a fault flag tested in mcu_0160_08003F2C. mcu_0160_08007DF4 both reads and writes it; its writer is not named yet.
